text:
Anthony Cirelli is the kind of center whose value hides in the parts of the game nobody puts on a highlight reel, and this season the hidden part is louder than usual. With him on the ice at 5-on-5, Tampa Bay takes 61% of the expected goals, a share that would make him one of the league's best play-drivers. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 95th percentile at creating chances last season after adjusting for teammates.

So why only 15 points in 21 games? Because the Lightning have scored 6.8 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him out there. That is the kind of gap that usually swings back. His own shooting runs the other way (6 goals on 4.44 expected, 20% on his shots), so call it a wash for goals and a debt owed on assists.

He missed time with an injury and returned on Nov. 17. Watch his entries: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him carrying the puck in 55% of the time, and 20% of his setups crossing the royal road. That's a two-time Stanley Cup winner still doing the hard things right.
